purpose: GOAL.md section 17's completion criterion: an explicit promote/do-not-promote decision for each filter family. Records conclusions only -- nothing is enabled.

families.name: Atomic manipulation / adjusted activity
families.rationale: The patterns ARE detectable -- `melt_atomic_scan.py` scanned all 45,609 tapes and independently reproduced 1.715% of transactions carrying >=2 same-side wallets, matching the earlier V3 measurement. But the family is confounded with activity at the label level (high-risk rate falls 0.9951 -> 0.5997 across n_swap quintiles, and n_swap alone separates the label at AUC 0.79), so separation collapses inside activity bands. Scored on REALISED net return under the deployed exit policy, and restricted to boundary-clean tokens, the F3 rungs worsen or do nothing -- none improves. Do not enable.

families.name: Entity-adjusted ownership concentration
families.rationale: The entity adjustment is REAL: merging same-transaction co-buyers changes the exact-volume holders-to-50% count for 37.75% of tokens (mean ratio 0.8806, zero monotonicity violations) and is 4x stronger on high-risk than low-risk. But it is not a filter -- on realised net return the two F4 rungs significantly WORSEN the median, and `ent_h50` scored worse than the baseline it was meant to improve. Do not enable.

families.name: Creator-cluster historical reputation
families.rationale: CORRECTED REASON. An earlier version of this record said F5 failed for 'no matured per-creator outcomes'. That was ASSERTED, not measured, and it is wrong about half the requirement: creator IDENTITY IS AVAILABLE -- `decisions.feature_json` carries `curve_creator` on 1,036 decisions across 768 distinct creators. What is missing is SUPPORT: only 53 creators ever reach a bought position (a matured outcome), 52 of them with exactly ONE, and NO creator has the 5+ matured outcomes a rate needs. So the verdict stands but the reason is sample size, not absent data. No decision is available; this is not a do-not-promote.

families.name: Historically informed-wallet flow
families.rationale: Needs forward markouts joined to a per-wallet history. MEASURED this round: the `trades` table carries NO wallet identity -- only the book's own fills (token, pool, px, pnl, position_id). So the bot cannot know which wallets traded, and the section-17 fixture category 'wallet skill / flow' is the ONLY one of ten with zero test evidence. The informed-wallet registry is additionally disabled as contaminated (4a.43). No decision is available; this is not a do-not-promote.

families.name: Manipulation-adjusted flow and breadth
families.rationale: Needs order-flow imbalance per entity with venue attribution. The tape gives per-token aggregates (signed per-wallet sums within a transaction), not an OFI series per entity over time, so the series F7 is defined on cannot be built from it. No decision is available.

families.name: Executable net value and exit capacity
families.rationale: Two findings, neither promotable. (1) CapacITY IS NOT the binding constraint at the deployed 0.01 SOL: the notional sits inside the observed trade-size spectrum for 99.98% of tokens and only 7 of 45,792 cannot absorb it from an entire hour of flow. (2) The net-return replay is NOT ADMISSIBLE: its take-profit engine is a migration-boundary artifact (take-profit tokens carry a 4.70x larger first-print/curve-price jump, and their first print sits BELOW their own median price). F8 cannot be promoted on evidence that cannot distinguish an edge from the boundary.

families.name: Calibration, prediction sets, abstention
families.rationale: The conformal gate is decisive on 0% of evaluations at EVERY alpha from 0.01 to 0.3 over 402 real outcomes, so there is no accepted subset to value and no accuracy/retention tradeoff to report. A gate that never acts cannot improve a policy. Do not enable.

families.name: Frozen candidate policy + fresh prospective cohort
families.rationale: Phase F item 4 / Phase G require ONE candidate policy frozen BEFORE a fresh prospective cohort. No such cohort exists and the current book is a development set. This is an OPERATOR act, not a research step.

families.name: Creator-SOLD exposure (not reputation)
families.rationale: The F5 measurement separated two features that had been conflated: creator REPUTATION needs history and has none, while creator-SOLD exposure needs no history and IS a recorded per-decision observable. It was recorded as a candidate and then EVALUATED, and the evaluation returns a bounded negative: on the bought population `dev_sell_share` is IDENTICALLY 0.0 (0 of 53 nonzero), so it is a CONSTANT and a constant carries no information -- this is not 'underpowered', it is categorically not evaluable as a predictor. The by-action distribution explains why: nonzero values live almost entirely in `skip` (590 of 922, 64.0%), while BOTH `reject` (0 of 63) and `buy` (0 of 55) are 0.0% -- so the creator-sold condition is resolved BEFORE the gates, not by them. A gate that already requires the creator to hold cannot be credited with the outcome difference later. NOT enabled, NOT promoted.

measurement_limits.detail: only 4.10% of decisions can ever link to an outcome, because a decision links only where the book bought; and the linkable subset is selected on p_rug/p_pump (the gates themselves)

measurement_limits.limit: first ~95-100 s of DEX trading is unobserved
measurement_limits.detail: the first post-migration print arrives a median 100 s after the last curve swap, so marks['60'] exists for 0 of 44,862 tokens and every take-profit lives inside that gap

measurement_limits.limit: no quotes anywhere in the corpus
measurement_limits.detail: the tapes hold EXECUTED trades, so depth-at-size, impact, slippage, fill probability and fees-at-size are unobservable -- this is what blocks Phase E items 1-3

measurement_limits.limit: no wallet identity on the book's trades
measurement_limits.detail: `trades` records the bot's own fills only, so per-wallet skill (F6) and section-17 category 6 have no data source
